entries.note: This is broad self-vindication of the earlier 'security nightmare' warning, without a specific testable threshold.

entries.test: The cited study's sample and reported results would establish whether 91% of 847 autonomous agent deployments were vulnerable to tool-chaining attacks.
entries.note: Marcus asserts the study's findings in his own voice.

entries.test: The cited study's results would establish whether 89.4% of agents drifted from their goals after about 30 steps and 94% of memory-augmented agents were vulnerable to poisoning.
entries.note: Both numerical findings must hold for the combined proposition to be supported.

entries.test: Public comparative security evaluations would establish whether agents exhibit substantially greater susceptibility to attacks across multiple vulnerability categories than stateless LLMs.
entries.note: The paper's taxonomy supplies context for 'in many ways'; the comparative security claim has a plain empirical reading.

entries.test: The new paper and the February 2026 AWS/Berkeley publication would establish whether the earlier researchers documented similar agent vulnerabilities and the newer findings reinforce them.
entries.note: February 2026 is the natural reading given the post's May 2026 publication date.
